scope: Theorem 9.1 (Marked words and a fixed middle arc) of the manuscript “Prefix Instructions and Incompressible Flows” (preprints/Prefix-Instructions-and-Incompressible-Flows-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8cd581420ec9967a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: This recorder gives an effective smooth mean-zero general force on the unit torus, with all mixed derivatives bounded and period one for t ≥ 1. Its unique classical periodic zero-data solution is global with bounded energy. The particle from (1/4, 1/4, 0) enters (1/2, 3/4) × T2 exactly when the machine halts. The repeated protocol uses only the table and initialization uses the input. Separately, one may choose either a solenoidal force with the same eventual periodicity, or a mean-zero force satisfying ∥f(t)∥Cm = O((1 + t)−1) for every spatial order m, with all mixed derivatives bounded and hence temporal L2 in every Cm norm. These two alternatives are separate prescriptions.
